literal: His father, seeking a strict tutor, had him beaten and whipped.
idiomatic: His father Yi, seeking a strict tutor, had him beaten and whipped.

literal: Ang did not follow his teacher's instructions; he devoted himself to riding and roaming, often saying, "A man ought to sweep across the world and seize wealth and rank for himself — who would sit upright reading books to become some old pedant?
idiomatic: Ang did not follow his teacher's instructions. He devoted himself to riding and roaming, often saying, "A man ought to sweep across the world and seize wealth and rank for himself — who would sit upright reading books to become some old pedant?

literal: With his elder brother Gan he repeatedly raided and plundered; no county or prefecture could bring them to justice.
idiomatic: With his elder brother Gan he repeatedly raided and plundered. No county or prefecture could bring them to justice.

literal: He gathered swordsmen, exhausting the family's wealth; the village folk feared him and none dared oppose him.
idiomatic: He gathered swordsmen until the family's wealth was spent. The village folk feared him, and none dared oppose him.

literal: His father Yi would often tell people, "This boy, far from destroying our clan, will enlarge our house — he is no mere local strongman.
idiomatic: His father Yi would often tell people, "This boy, far from destroying our clan, will enlarge our house — he is no mere local strongman.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi the brothers together raised troops; afterward, obeying an imperial order, they dispersed their followers. Ang was then made attendant-in-ordinary in regular attendance on the cavalry and enfeoffed Baron of Wucheng County with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi the brothers together raised troops. Obeying an imperial order, they dispersed their followers. Ang was then made attendant-in-ordinary in regular attendance on the cavalry and enfeoffed baron of Wucheng County with a fief of five hundred households.

literal: Gan resigned his office and returned; together with Ang he remained in their home district, secretly training bold warriors.
idiomatic: Gan resigned his office and returned home. Together with Ang he remained in their district, secretly training bold warriors.

literal: Erzhu Rong, hearing of this, took a dislike to them and secretly ordered Prefect Yuan Zhongzong to lure and seize Ang, sending him to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, hearing of this, took a dislike to them and secretly ordered Prefect Yuan Zhongzong to lure and seize Ang, sending him to Jinyang.

literal: At the end of Yongan, Rong entered Luoyang and brought Ang with him, imprisoning him at the Camel-and-Ox Office.
idiomatic: At the end of Yongan, Rong entered Luoyang and brought Ang with him, imprisoning him at the Camel-and-Ox Office.

literal: Not long afterward Rong died, and Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei received Ang in audience and comforted and encouraged him.
idiomatic: Not long afterward Rong died. Emperor Xiaozhuang received Ang in audience and comforted and encouraged him.

literal: At that time the Erzhu faction, having grown powerful, again pressed on the palace gates; the emperor personally came to the Great Xia Gate to command and direct dispositions.
idiomatic: At that time the Erzhu faction, grown powerful, again pressed on the palace gates. The emperor personally came to the Great Xia Gate to command and direct dispositions.

literal: Ang, now freed from his bonds, donned armor and grasped his halberd, his spirit soaring above fierce foes.
idiomatic: Ang, now freed from his bonds, donned armor and grasped his halberd, his spirit soaring above the fiercest foes.

literal: He then drove forward with his nephew Changming and others at the spearhead; wherever they went, none could withstand them.
idiomatic: He then drove forward with his nephew Changming and others at the spearhead. Wherever they struck, none could stand.

literal: The emperor and all who watched were impressed by his valor.
idiomatic: The emperor and all who watched were struck by his valor.

literal: He was immediately made general of the straight gate and granted a thousand bolts of silk.
idiomatic: He was immediately made general of the straight gate and granted a thousand bolts of silk.

literal: Ang reasoned that the calamity of invasion was still severe and no one man could remedy it; he therefore asked to return to his home district and gather his retainers.
idiomatic: Ang reasoned that the calamity of invasion was still severe and no one man could remedy it. He therefore asked to return to his home district and gather his retainers.

literal: He was also made attendant-in-ordinary in regular attendance and additionally given the title general who pacifies the north.
idiomatic: He was also made attendant-in-ordinary in regular attendance and additionally given the title general who pacifies the north.

literal: Brave volunteers everywhere raced to join him.
idiomatic: Brave volunteers everywhere raced to join him.

literal: Soon the capital fell; he then joined his father and brothers in raising the righteous banner at Xindu.
idiomatic: Soon the capital fell. He then joined his father and brothers in raising the righteous banner at Xindu.

literal: Erzhu Yusheng, governor of Yinzhou, sent troops in a stealth attack that suddenly reached the city walls. Ang had no time to don armor; with just over ten riders he galloped forth, and Yusheng retreated — the people's hearts were thus settled.
idiomatic: Erzhu Yusheng, governor of Yinzhou, sent troops in a stealth attack that suddenly reached the city walls. Ang had no time to don armor. With just over ten riders he galloped forth, and Yusheng retreated — the people's hearts were thus settled.

literal: When the Deposed Emperor was established, Ang was made bearer of the staff, governor of Ji Province — an office he held for life.
idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor was established, Ang was made bearer of the staff and governor of Ji Province — an office he held for life.

literal: He also served as grand commander, leading troops to follow Gao Huan in defeating Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a.
idiomatic: He also served as grand commander, leading troops to follow Gao Huan in defeating Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a.

literal: When Ye was pacified, he separately led his own forces to hold Liyang.
idiomatic: When Ye was pacified, he separately led his own forces to hold Liyang.

literal: He again followed Gao Huan in campaigning against Erzhu Zhao at Hanling; Ang personally led three thousand men from his home district's retinue — Wang Taotang, Dongfang Lao, Huyan Zu, and others.
idiomatic: He again followed Gao Huan in campaigning against Erzhu Zhao at Hanling. Ang personally led three thousand men from his home district's retinue — Wang Taotang, Dongfang Lao, Huyan Zu, and others.

literal: Gao Huan said, "Commander Gao will lead only Han men — I fear that will not suffice. Now we should assign more than a thousand Xianbei soldiers to be mixed among them. What do you think of this?
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Commander Gao will lead only Han men — I fear that will not suffice. Now we should assign more than a thousand Xianbei soldiers to be mixed among them. What do you think of this?

literal: " Ang replied, "The retainers I, Aocao, command have long been drilled; in battle after battle they are no less than the Xianbei. If we mix the forces now, their spirits will not unite — in victory they will quarrel over credit, in retreat they will blame one another. I wish to lead Han troops alone and need no further reassignment.
idiomatic: " Ang replied, "The retainers I, Aocao, command have long been drilled. In battle after battle they are no less than the Xianbei. If we mix the forces now, their spirits will not unite — in victory they will quarrel over credit, in retreat they will blame one another. I wish to lead Han troops alone and need no further reassignment.

literal: " Gao Huan approved.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan approved.

literal: When battle was joined, Gao Huan fared poorly; the army fell back slightly, and Zhao and his men were just pressing their advantage.
idiomatic: When battle was joined, Gao Huan fared poorly. The army fell back slightly, and Zhao and his men were just pressing their advantage.

literal: Gao Yue, Han the Xiongnu, and others charged their front with five hundred cavalry; Hulü Dun gathered the scattered troops and pursued from the rear; Ang and Cai Jun came out from Liyuan with a thousand riders and struck Zhao's army on the flank.
idiomatic: Gao Yue, Han the Xiongnu, and others charged their front with five hundred cavalry. Hulü Dun gathered the scattered troops and pursued from the rear. Ang and Cai Jun came out from Liyuan with a thousand riders and struck Zhao's army on the flank.

literal: Zhao's host was utterly routed.
idiomatic: Zhao's host was utterly routed.

literal: That day, without Ang and the others, Gao Huan would have perished.
idiomatic: That day, without Ang and the others, Gao Huan would have perished.

literal: At that time Gao Huan was occupied with affairs in Guan and Long; he made Ang grand commander on the southwestern route, pressing straight toward Shangluo.
idiomatic: At that time Gao Huan was occupied with affairs in Guan and Long. He made Ang grand commander on the southwestern route, pressing straight toward Shangluo.

literal: The mountain roads were steep and narrow; the enemy already held the passes. Ang fought his way forward — none could stand against his spearhead.
idiomatic: The mountain roads were steep and narrow, and the enemy already held the passes. Ang fought his way forward — none could stand against his spearhead.

literal: He then captured Shangluo, taking Western Wei governor of Luo Province Quan Qi along with several dozen other commanders.
idiomatic: He then captured Shangluo, taking Western Wei governor of Luo Province Quan Qi along with several dozen other commanders.

literal: When Dou Tai suffered defeat, Ang was recalled to withdraw his troops.
idiomatic: When Dou Tai suffered defeat, Ang was recalled to withdraw his troops.

literal: By then Ang had been struck by a stray arrow; his wound was grave. He turned to those beside him and said, "I have given my body to the state — I die without regret. All I lament is that I shall not live to see Jishi made governor.
idiomatic: By then Ang had been struck by a stray arrow. His wound was grave. He turned to those beside him and said, "I have given my body to the state — I die without regret. All I lament is that I shall not live to see Jishi made governor.

literal: " When Gao Huan heard this, he immediately sent a courier to appoint Jishi governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: " When Gao Huan heard this, he immediately sent a courier to appoint Jishi governor of Ji Province.

literal: After Ang returned, he again served as grand commander of the army staff, supervising seventy-six area commanders, and with mobile-circuit commissioner Hou Jing drilled troops at Wulao.
idiomatic: After Ang returned, he again served as grand commander of the army staff, supervising seventy-six area commanders, and with mobile-circuit commissioner Hou Jing drilled troops at Wulao.

literal: Censor-in-chief Liu Gui at that time also led troops in Northern Yu Province; he and Ang had a minor quarrel. Ang flew into a rage, beat the drums to muster his men, and attacked him.
idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Liu Gui at that time also led troops in Northern Yu Province. He and Ang had a minor quarrel. Ang flew into a rage, beat the drums to muster his men, and attacked him.

literal: Hou Jing and Ji Province governor Moqi Shouluogan came to the rescue and only then was it stopped.
idiomatic: Hou Jing and Ji Province governor Moqi Shouluogan came to the rescue, and only then was it stopped.

literal: Such was the lordly, confrontational spirit with which he towered over others.
idiomatic: Such was the swaggering boldness with which he towered over all around him.

literal: At that time the Xianbei jointly looked down on Chinese court officials — only Ang they feared and obeyed.
idiomatic: At that time the Xianbei jointly looked down on Chinese court officials — only Ang they feared and obeyed.

literal: Whenever Gao Huan addressed the three armies, he usually spoke in Xianbei; but if Ang was present in the ranks, he used Chinese.
idiomatic: Whenever Gao Huan addressed the three armies, he usually spoke in Xianbei. But if Ang was present in the ranks, he used Chinese.

literal: Once Ang went to the chief minister's headquarters; the gatekeeper would not admit him. Ang grew angry and strung his bow to shoot the man.
idiomatic: Once Ang went to the chief minister's headquarters. The gatekeeper would not admit him. Ang grew angry and strung his bow to shoot the man.

literal: Gao Huan knew of it but did not punish him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan knew of it but did not punish him.

literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang, his rank was advanced to Duke of Jingzhao Commandery with a fief of a thousand households.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxiang his rank was advanced to duke of Jingzhao Commandery with a fief of a thousand households.

literal: Together with Hou Jing and the others he besieged Dugu Ruyuan at Jinyong city; Yuwen Tai led troops to the rescue.
idiomatic: Together with Hou Jing and the others he besieged Dugu Ruyuan at Jinyong city. Yuwen Tai led troops to the rescue.

literal: They fought at the north bank of the Mang; Ang's command faltered, his attendants scattered. He rode alone eastward, intending to reach the south wall of Heyang — the gate was closed and he could not enter, and he was killed by Western troops. He was forty-eight.
idiomatic: They fought at the north bank of the Mang. Ang's command faltered and his attendants scattered. He rode alone eastward, intending to reach the south wall of Heyang — the gate was closed and he could not enter, and Western troops killed him. He was forty-eight.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin, grand tutor, grand marshal, grand commandant, director of the Masters of Writing, and governor of Ji Province — posthumous title Zhongwu.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin, grand tutor, grand marshal, grand commandant, director of the masters of writing, and governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Zhongwu.

literal: His son Tuqi succeeded but died young.
idiomatic: His son Tuqi succeeded but died young.

literal: Gao Cheng summoned Ang's sons again and personally selected his third son Daohuo to succeed.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng summoned Ang's sons again and personally selected his third son Daohuo to succeed.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, Ang was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yongchang.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian, Ang was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of Yongchang.

literal: Daohuo inherited the title; at the end of Wuping he was made opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.
idiomatic: Daohuo inherited the title. At the end of Wuping he was made opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.

literal: After submitting to Zhou, he was granted the title of general equal in protocol to three imperators.
idiomatic: After submitting to Zhou, he was granted the title of general equal in protocol to three imperators.

literal: During the Kaihuang era he died while serving as governor of Huangzhou.
idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era he died while serving as governor of Huangzhou.

literal: Jishi, styled Zitong, was Gan's fourth younger brother.
idiomatic: Jishi, styled Zitong, was Gan's fourth younger brother.

literal: He too possessed courage and boldness.
idiomatic: He too possessed courage and boldness.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was appointed general who pacifies the distance and regular attendant; transferred to general of the guard and grand master for the golden seal and purple ribbon; soon additionally made attendant cavalier at attendance in regular succession and put in charge of the directorate of imperial robes.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was appointed general who pacifies the distance and regular attendant, transferred to general of the guard and grand master for the golden seal and purple ribbon, and soon additionally made attendant cavalier at attendance in regular succession and put in charge of the directorate of imperial robes.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made director of imperial provisions.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was made director of imperial provisions.

literal: During Tianping he went out as governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: During Tianping he went out as governor of Ji Province.

literal: The old bandits of Shandong — Liu Pantuo, Shi Mingyao, and others — attacked travelers on the roads and raided villages and towns; the four provinces of Qi, Yan, Qing, and Xu suffered from them, yet successive administrations could not subdue them.
idiomatic: The old bandits of Shandong — Liu Pantuo, Shi Mingyao, and others — attacked travelers on the roads and raided villages and towns. The four provinces of Qi, Yan, Qing, and Xu suffered from them, yet successive administrations could not subdue them.

literal: When Jishi arrived, he destroyed them all.
idiomatic: When Jishi arrived, he destroyed them all.

literal: Soon thereafter the Puyang commoner Du Lingchun and others assaulted cities and pillaged the countryside, gathering a crowd of nearly ten thousand. Jishi sent three hundred cavalry and captured them in a single battle.
idiomatic: Soon thereafter the Puyang commoner Du Lingchun and others assaulted cities and pillaged the countryside, gathering a crowd of nearly ten thousand. Jishi sent three hundred cavalry and captured them in a single battle.

literal: Also, the Yangping partisan Luo Shuwen's follower Xu Xian and others erected stockades in rebellion — Jishi crushed them.
idiomatic: Also, the Yangping partisan Luo Shuwen's follower Xu Xian and others erected stockades in rebellion — Jishi crushed them.

literal: Again, a band of robbers broke through Nanhe Commandery; Jishi sent troops against them and beheaded the lot without delay.
idiomatic: Again, a band of robbers broke through Nanhe Commandery. Jishi sent troops against them and beheaded the lot without delay.

literal: From then on, far and near enjoyed peace and order.
idiomatic: From then on, far and near enjoyed peace and order.

literal: Jishi and his brothers were exalted and prosperous, each with distinction in their time; Jishi personally led more than a thousand retainers, eight hundred horses, and full armor and weapons — hence whenever he pursued and suppressed bandits, he more often than not won decisive victories.
idiomatic: Jishi and his brothers were exalted and prosperous, each with distinction in their time. Jishi personally led more than a thousand retainers, eight hundred horses, and full armor and weapons — hence whenever he pursued and suppressed bandits, he more often than not won decisive victories.

literal: A guest once said to Jishi, "Puyang and Yangping lie within the capital region. They neither obey orders nor cross your borders — what urgency is there to send private troops on a distant campaign?
idiomatic: A guest once said to Jishi, "Puyang and Yangping lie within the capital region. They neither obey orders nor cross your borders — what urgency is there to send private troops on a distant campaign?

literal: If you fail and are caught, will you not invite punishment?
idiomatic: If you fail and are caught, will you not invite punishment?

literal: " Jishi said, "Your words are deeply disloyal!
idiomatic: " Jishi said, "Your words are deeply disloyal!

literal: I and the state share one fate in weal and woe — how could I see bandits and not strike them down?
idiomatic: I and the state share one fate in weal and woe — how could I see bandits and not strike them down?

literal: Besides, the bandits know the court's army cannot come in time and do not suspect rescue from another province. Before they are prepared, we can surely break them.
idiomatic: Besides, the bandits know the court's army cannot come in time and do not suspect rescue from another province. Before they are prepared, we can surely break them.

literal: War favors speed — why wait for a slower hand? If I am punished for this, I shall have no regret.
idiomatic: War favors speed — why wait for a slower hand? If I am punished for this, I shall have no regret.

literal: During Yuanxiang, Western invaders arrived in force.
idiomatic: During Yuanxiang, Western invaders arrived in force.

literal: Gao Huan personally led the three armies to meet them and formed battle lines north of the Mang; the army suffered a great defeat — corpses floated down the river in unbroken succession, and routed troops stretched from van to rear without end.
idiomatic: Gao Huan personally led the three armies to meet them and formed battle lines north of the Mang. The army suffered a great defeat — corpses floated down the river in unbroken succession, and routed troops stretched from van to rear without end.

literal: Hearts everywhere were stirred; people spoke of the world's difficulties.
idiomatic: Hearts everywhere were stirred. People spoke of the world's difficulties.

literal: Jishi's trusted retainers urged him, "Today's situation is lost. Take two hundred of your closest riders and flee to Liang — you will escape disaster and keep your wealth and rank.
idiomatic: Jishi's trusted retainers urged him, "Today's situation is lost. Take two hundred of your closest riders and flee to Liang — you will escape disaster and keep your wealth and rank.

literal: Why sit here and wait for death?
idiomatic: Why sit here and wait for death?

literal: " Jishi said, "My brothers and I have received the state's deep favor. Together with the Lord Gao we settled the realm. Now that all is collapsing, to flee would be unrighteous.
idiomatic: " Jishi said, "My brothers and I have received the state's deep favor. Together with Gao Huan we settled the realm. Now that all is collapsing, to flee would be unrighteous.

literal: If the altars are overturned, I shall die fighting with my back to the wall — how could I steal my life away in petty survival?
idiomatic: If the altars are overturned, I shall die fighting with my back to the wall — how could I steal my life away in petty survival?

literal: " In this campaign the minister over the masses fell.
idiomatic: " In this campaign the minister over the masses fell.

literal: He entered the capital as attendant cavalier at attendance in regular succession.
idiomatic: He entered the capital as attendant cavalier at attendance in regular succession.

literal: During Xinghe he administered Jin Province affairs.
idiomatic: During Xinghe he administered Jin Province affairs.

literal: He relinquished the province but continued to garrison Yong'an fortress.
idiomatic: He relinquished the province but continued to garrison Yong'an fortress.

literal: Gao Shen rebelled at Wulao and sent a messenger to inform Jishi.
idiomatic: Gao Shen rebelled at Wulao and sent a messenger to inform Jishi.

literal: Jishi, reading the letter, was alarmed and frightened; he immediately fled in disarray to report to Gao Huan.
idiomatic: Jishi, reading the letter, was alarmed and frightened. He immediately fled in disarray to report to Gao Huan.

literal: Gao Huan praised his utmost loyalty and treated him as before.
idiomatic: Gao Huan praised his utmost loyalty and treated him as before.

literal: During Wuding he was made palace attendant; soon additionally made chief rectifier of Ji Province — at the time Gao Cheng had previously held this post and memorialized to have it transferred back to Jishi.
idiomatic: During Wuding he was made palace attendant and soon additionally made chief rectifier of Ji Province. Gao Cheng had previously held this post and memorialized to have it transferred back to Jishi.

literal: As area commander, he followed the Duke of Qinghe, Yue, in defeating Xiao Ming at Hanshan and Hou Jing at Woyang.
idiomatic: As area commander, he followed the Duke of Qinghe, Yue, in defeating Xiao Ming at Hanshan and Hou Jing at Woyang.

literal: On his return he was made director of the court of imperial stud.
idiomatic: On his return he was made director of the court of imperial stud.

literal: Again serving as area commander, he followed the Duke of Qinghe in attacking Wang Si'en at Yingchuan and took the city.
idiomatic: Again serving as area commander, he followed the Duke of Qinghe in attacking Wang Si'en at Yingchuan and took the city.

literal: For his cumulative merits he was additionally granted equal in protocol to three imperators.
idiomatic: For his cumulative merits he was additionally granted equal in protocol to three imperators.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chengshi County.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as viscount of Chengshi County.

literal: He continued as area commander, following Minister over the Masses Pan Yue in campaigning between the Yangtze and Huai.
idiomatic: He continued as area commander, following Minister over the Masses Pan Yue in campaigning between the Yangtze and Huai.

literal: He privately sent musicians to trade at the border; on returning to the capital he was detained on that charge, but was soon pardoned.
idiomatic: He privately sent musicians to trade at the border. On returning to the capital he was detained on that charge, but was soon pardoned.

literal: In the fourth summer of his tenure, he died of a carbuncle. He was thirty-eight.
idiomatic: In the fourth summer he died of a carbuncle. He was thirty-eight.

literal: Posthumously granted palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Cang and Ji provinces, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and governor of Ji Province — posthumous title Gongmu.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Cang and Ji provinces, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Gongmu.

literal: Jishi was bold and unrestrained, fond of wine; he also relied on his family's collective merits and observed no restraint in conduct.
idiomatic: Jishi was bold and unrestrained, fond of wine. He also relied on his family's collective merits and observed no restraint in conduct.

literal: He and Guangzhou governor Li Yuanzhong had been close friends all their lives. While drinking one night in Ji Province, he thought of Yuanzhong — opened the city gates and had attendants take post-horses carrying a jar of wine to Guang Province to share a cup with Yuanzhong.
idiomatic: He and Guangzhou governor Li Yuanzhong had been close friends all their lives. While drinking one night in Ji Province, he thought of Yuanzhong — opened the city gates and had attendants take post-horses carrying a jar of wine to Guang Province to share a cup with Yuanzhong.

literal: The court knew of it but indulged him.
idiomatic: The court knew of it but indulged him.
